# Data Preparation

First, we prepare the working environment.

```{r}
rm(list=ls()) # Clear the environment
# setwd("...")  # Setup the working directory
```

### Installation

Install the jpeg package which we will use for analysis.
```{r}
#install.packages("jpeg")
library(jpeg)
# ?readJPEG
# install.packages("grid")
library(grid)
```

This reads the original image. It reads it into an array of size `417 x 542`.
```{r}
Buda <- readJPEG("Buda.jpg")
str(Buda)
# grid.raster(Buda)
```

![](Buda.jpg)

This is a grayscale image where each pixel has an intensity value between 0 and 1.
```{r}
min(Buda)
max(Buda)
```

# Singular value decomposition

We will now perform a SVD on this matrix. This creates three objects, namely, `d` consisting of singular values (417), `u` consisting of left singular vectors (417 * 417), and `v` consisting of right singular vectors (542 * 417). Notice that `v` is not 542*542 as R provides economy SVD for only non 0 sigular values. 
```{r}
?svd
s <- svd(Buda[,])
str(s)
```
Let us now develop a low rank approximation. As we see the singular values have a few high values and then it quickly drops off.
```{r}
plot(s$d)
```

Let us create a rank one approximation to the matrix using only the first singular value/vector
```{r}
s1 <- s$d[1]*s$u[,1]%*%t(s$v[,1])
str(s1)
?writeJPEG
writeJPEG(s1,"Buda1.jpg")
# Buda1 <- readJPEG("Buda1.jpg")
# grid.raster(Buda1)
```
![](Buda1.jpg)

Let us create a rank ten approximation to the matrix

```{r}
s10 <- s$u[,1:10]%*%diag(s$d[1:10])%*%t(s$v[,1:10])
str(s10)
writeJPEG(s10,"Buda10.jpg")
Buda10 <- readJPEG("Buda10.jpg")
# grid.raster(Buda10)
```
![](Buda10.jpg)

```{r}
s100 <- s$u[,1:100]%*%diag(s$d[1:100])%*%t(s$v[,1:100])
str(s100)
writeJPEG(s100,"Buda100.jpg")
Buda100 <- readJPEG("Buda100.jpg")
# grid.raster(Buda100)
```
![](Buda100.jpg)

Let's see the proportion of information (variance) retained by the rank-$k$ approximation.

```{r}
var <- cumsum(s$d^2) # [\sigma_1^2, \sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2, \sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2+\sigma_3^2, ...]
str(var)
plot(1:length(s$d),var/max(var))
var[1]/max(var)
var[10]/max(var)
var[100]/max(var)
```

The first singular value accounts for 87.37%, the first ten singular values account for 96.48%, and the first hundred singular values account for 99.79%.  

# RGB Image

We now repeat the analysis using an RGB image. 

```{r}
Labubu <- readJPEG("Labubu.jpg")
str(Labubu)
```
![](Labubu.jpg)


This is read into an array of size 736 x 736 x 3 
(height × width × channels). The three channels store the RGB color intensities.

# Note that in this case Labubu[,,1] is different from Labubu[,,2] and Labubu[,,3].


Let's now perform the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on the different channels
```{r}
s1 <- svd(Labubu[,,1])
s2 <- svd(Labubu[,,2])
s3 <- svd(Labubu[,,3])
```

Develop low rank approximation (with rank 50). Initialize the vector for storing the approximation
```{r}
Labubu50 <- array(dim=c(736,736,3))
Labubu50[,,1] <- s1$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s1$d[1:50])%*%t(s1$v[,1:50])
Labubu50[,,2] <- s2$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s2$d[1:50])%*%t(s2$v[,1:50])
Labubu50[,,3] <- s3$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s3$d[1:50])%*%t(s3$v[,1:50])
```

```{r}
writeJPEG(Labubu50,"Labubu50.jpg")
```
![](Labubu50.jpg)

Let's retry with a higher approximation using 400 singular values/vectors.

```{r}
Labubu400 <- array(dim=c(736,736,3))
Labubu400[,,1] <- s1$u[,1:400]%*%diag(s1$d[1:400])%*%t(s1$v[,1:400])
Labubu400[,,2] <- s2$u[,1:400]%*%diag(s2$d[1:400])%*%t(s2$v[,1:400])
Labubu400[,,3] <- s3$u[,1:400]%*%diag(s3$d[1:400])%*%t(s3$v[,1:400])
writeJPEG(Labubu400,"Labubu400.jpg") # --> much better!
```
![](Labubu400.jpg)

#### End of notes
